title: Fewest Notes, Two Denominations
src: MathWorks OA, IIT Bombay, 2026 (Embedded Systems role, HackerRank). Coding question 2 of 2. The reported statement was garbled; the samples show the answer is the smallest a + b.
body:
You are given the values arr (think of them as banknote denominations, each available in unlimited supply), a list of amounts query, and an integer k.

For each amount x, find non-negative integers a, b and indices i, j with

a · arr[i] + b · arr[j] = x and a + b ≤ k,

so that a + b is as small as possible. In other words, pay x with at most k notes taken from at most two denominations, using as few notes as possible.

Output that smallest a + b for every query, or -1 if the amount can't be paid.
inp: Line 1: n and k. Line 2: the n values of arr. Line 3: q. Line 4: the q amounts.
out: q integers on one line, separated by spaces.

samples.ex: 1 = 1·1 (one note). 4 = 2·2 or 1 + 3 (two notes). 30 = 5·6 (five notes; four notes reach at most 24 without 67). 70 = 67 + 3 (two notes). 89 can't be paid with at most 5 notes from two denominations.
13 = 10 + 3 (two notes). 40 = 4·10 (four notes). 41 = 2·10 + 7·3 needs nine notes, more than k = 4. 7 can't be made from 10s and 3s at all.

lc: 322 Coin Change (related; Codeforces 529D / 524C is the exact problem)

stub.py:
import sys

def fewest_notes(arr, k, queries):
    # return one answer per query, -1 when the amount cannot be paid
    return [-1] * len(queries)

def main():
    data = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
    n, k = data[0], data[1]
    arr = data[2:2 + n]
    p = 2 + n
    q = data[p]
    queries = data[p + 1:p + 1 + q]
    print(" ".join(map(str, fewest_notes(arr, k, queries))))

main()
